newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-THOMPSON, WALKER WIN TWO GOLDS EACH.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-THOMPSON, WALKER WIN TWO GOLDS EACH.

text.p: Americans Neil Walker and Jenny Thompson outshone two of Australia's youth brigade by winning two gold medals each at the Pan Pacific championships on Tuesday,
Overall, Americans won five of the eight golds contested with Walker breaking an 11-year-old U.S. record in the men's 100 butterfly and also anchoring the U.S. relay team to victory.
His butterfly time of 52.76 seconds broke the old record of 52.84 set by Pablo Morales in 1986.
"It was a great swim. I just wanted to go out fast and fight off Klim at the end," Walker, 21, said.
Australian Michael Klim finished second in 52.94.
Thompson caught Japan's Ayari Aoyama in the last five metres to win the women's 100 butterfly in 59.00, the best time this year.
Aoyama, who uses a submarine start, led by half a body length at the turn, but faded to finish in 59.35. Thompson said she is no longer intimidated by opponents who use submarine starts.
"They used to make me nervous, but not anymore," she said.
A five-times Olympic champion, Thompson also anchored the U.S. to victory in the women's 4x100 freestyle, her second gold of the day and fourth of the meet.
Russian-born Lenny Krayzelburg won the fifth U.S. gold in the men's 200 backstroke in 1:57.87, the fifth-fastest ever in the distance.
Australia's youth brigade of Grant Hackett and Ian Thorpe blazed to a one-two finish in the men's 400 metres freestyle.

Hackett, 17, won in three minutes 47.27 seconds, the ninth fastest time ever and the fastest this year, but said he is already looking over his shoulder at the 14-year-old Thorpe, who finished in 3:49.64.
"I'm young, but he's amazing," Hackett said about Thorpe, who has already cut 14 seconds off his personal best this year.
"The young guns took me to school," said American third-place finisher Chad Carvin, who is 23.
Olympic champion Danyon Loader of New Zeland finished more than five seconds behind Thorpe in fifth place.
Japan's Mai Nakamura repeated her gold medal-winning performance in the women's 100 backstroke by taking the 200 backstroke ahead of Lea Loveless-Maurer of the United States.
Costa Rica's Claudia Poll swam the fastest women's 400 freestyle in four years. Her time of 4:06.56 was better than the gold-medal time of 4:07.25 set by Ireland's Michelle Smith in Atlanta.
Poll also swam the third-fastest time ever to win the 200 freestyle on Sunday.
